article_notes: Russian methodological guidelines (LLM translation, not reviewed). B. canis babesiosis in central Russia, diagnosis by blood smear and serology (indirect haemagglutination); sources are veterinary station reports and the university parasitology laboratory, so setting is mixed. Disease forms (severe, moderate, mild; also hyperacute, acute, chronic, latent) are not defined and the numbers of dogs per form are not given. All severity findings are narrative: parasitaemia ranges by form, age groups, and the direction of haematological and biochemical changes in the severe form (fold changes vs normal), with no test, so every row is descriptive_only with low confidence. Not extracted: seasonal and immunity statements (no marker), breed (hyperacute form noted in Labrador, East European Shepherd and spaniel, anecdotal with no comparison), drug efficacy results (treatment response).

severity_definitions.label: severe form vs moderate and mild forms
severity_definitions.definition: Clinical forms of the disease (severe, moderately severe, moderate, mild) as graded by the authors; criteria not stated. For parasitaemia, the severe group is severe or moderately severe and the comparison is mild course.
severity_definitions.comparison_group: moderate and mild forms (n not stated)
severity_definitions.quote: In moderate and mild disease, the above-mentioned hematological and biochemical changes in dogs are less pronounced.

associations.statistic: severe or moderately severe: УП = 23-68%; mild course: 2,5-7%
associations.quote: with manifestation of the disease in a severe or moderately severe form in a small number of dogs of the urban population (УП=23-68%). Low and average parasitemia values (2,5-7%) are noted in the same seasons in most of the infected animals (more than 80%). In these cases the disease takes a mild course.
associations.note: Ranges of parasitaemia by disease form; no group sizes, no test. The same paragraph states that parasitaemia correlates with severity across years. Severe group includes moderately severe dogs. Translated text.

associations.quote: Dogs aged one to two years are often infected with babesias (more than 40%) and the disease in them takes a more severe form compared with animals aged 3-7 years.
associations.location: Results and discussion, para on age
associations.note: U-shaped: more severe disease in dogs aged 1-2 years and moderate and severe disease predominating in dogs aged 13-17 years, mostly mild or moderate in dogs aged 3-7 years. No group sizes, no test. Translated text.

associations.quote: in dogs with the severe form of babesiosis there are erythropenia, decreased hemoglobin, hematocrit and platelets, leukocytosis, increased blood concentrations of bilirubin (3-25-fold), urea (1,5-5), creatinine (1,2-3)
associations.location: Results and discussion, para on haematological and biochemical studies
associations.note: Direction stated for the severe form only; the text says these changes are less pronounced in moderate and mild disease (the abstract says not significant), with no values for the milder groups, no group sizes and no test. Translated text (from Russian).
